strings.name: Ashish Vaswani
strings.summary: Ashish Vaswani is an India-born computer scientist who published the Transformer paper with seven collaborators in 2017. Its attention-based approach to sequence modeling became an important foundation for later language models. He researched at Google Brain and co-founded Adept and Essential AI, pursuing model research and applications. These were collective achievements; being the first-listed author does not mean he invented the architecture alone.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026; selected education, research and entrepreneurial milestones. His birth year is not reliably established. The 2026 NVIDIA move is attributed to reporting and does not establish that an acquisition of the entire company was completed.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped introduce the Transformer architecture, advancing the technical foundations of natural language processing and large generative models.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a computer science PhD at the University of Southern California in 2014.
strings.facts.f2.label: Birth year
strings.facts.f2.value: Award biographical material and a public biography disagree; the year is not reliably established and is left unspecified.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Co-introducing the Transformer
strings.highlights.h1.text: As one of eight authors, proposed an attention-centered sequence model supporting more parallel training and influencing later language models.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Open-model research
strings.highlights.h2.text: Promoted open-model work at Essential AI and authored the 2025 introduction to the team’s Rnj-1 base and instruction-tuned models.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Media reports a move to NVIDIA
strings.timeline.t1.text: Ground Level AI reports that he and several Essential AI colleagues joined NVIDIA; the report also preserves uncertainty over whether the deal was finalized.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Introduces Rnj-1
strings.timeline.t2.text: In a signed article, presents the team’s eight-billion-parameter base and instruction-tuned models and outlines an open-research direction.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Transformer team named prize recipients
strings.timeline.t3.text: The NEC C&C Foundation announces the C&C Prize for the team of eight paper authors, recognizing their collective research contribution.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Essential AI announces funding
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company release names him and Niki Parmar as co-founders and announces a $56.5 million Series A; this entry uses the announcement date.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Adept makes its public introduction
strings.timeline.t5.text: Co-founder David Luan confirms Vaswani’s founding role in the company introduction and describes research into AI operating software tools.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Co-authors the Transformer paper
strings.timeline.t6.text: Publishes Attention Is All You Need with seven collaborators, studying an attention architecture without recurrence or convolution on machine translation tasks.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Google Brain
strings.timeline.t7.text: Works as a research scientist, undertaking research that later leads to the Transformer paper and exploring language models with colleagues.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earns a computer science doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completes his doctorate at the University of Southern California, with research experience in natural language processing and neural language models.
